subject.title: chatCompletions: ignore request model when x-openclaw-agent-id header is present

question: Should a valid `x-openclaw-agent-id` make OpenAI-compatible requests ignore or tolerate a generic body `model`, or should the body `model` continue to be an OpenClaw agent-target id?
rationale: The implementation is bounded, but the choice changes a documented public gateway API contract and needs parity across Chat Completions, Responses, and embeddings.

options.title: Adopt header precedence
options.body: Allow generic body model strings as compatibility metadata when a valid agent header selects the agent, and document/test the exact endpoint set covered.

options.title: Preserve agent-first model contract
options.body: Keep requiring `model` to be `openclaw`, `openclaw/default`, or `openclaw/<agentId>`, and steer SDK integrations to those ids plus `x-openclaw-model` for backend overrides.

options.title: Decide shared OpenAI-compatible semantics first
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose one precedence rule for Chat Completions, Responses, and embeddings.

recommendation.title: Decide shared OpenAI-compatible semantics first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose one precedence rule for Chat Completions, Responses, and embeddings.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc introduced the agent-first contract this issue would modify and is the clearest routing candidate for the product/API decision.
